claim: Mood is scene-level emotional colour — the same tone played in a different room — biasing tags, grade, music and lighting together. Where tone sets the film's key, mood decides whether this particular scene is lonely or euphoric, and it is the fastest handle when a scene reads flat.
method: identical subject sentence and seed in every panel; only the option clause changes. panels marked control render the untouched subject, because SDXL cannot express absence.

panels.clause: neutral expression, even balanced lighting, natural colors
warm color palette, golden glow, cozy light
hopeful, soft smile, bright rising light, luminous
lonely, solitary figure, empty surrounding space, cold muted palette
anxious, worried expression, sweating, restless unease
grieving, tears, hollow expression, drained color
angry, furrowed brow, red hot tones, harsh contrast
euphoric, ecstatic expression, blown-out bright light, saturated color
numb, blank expression, flat dull lighting, desaturated
nostalgic, faded warm colors, soft haze, film grain
ominous, encroaching shadow, cold blue cast, foreboding
intimate, quiet warmth, soft close glow, hushed
chaotic, clashing colors, cluttered frenetic energy
